Hi,

this is unrelated to aroma.affymetrix but rather a problem with the
'sift' package. I don't know what is going on, but let's start
troubleshooting by trying to get the following to work:

Start a fresh R session, e.g. Rterm --vanilla, and see what you get if you do:

library(sfit)
example(cfit.matrix)

If that gives an error, which I guess from you current report, what
output do you get from:

fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98, verbose=TRUE)

/Henrik

parts:
Hi,

> library(sfit)
> example(cfit.matrix)
 
works fine with no error message.
 

> example(cfit.matrix)

cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> # Simulate data
cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> N <- 1000

cft.mt> # Simulate genotypes
cft.mt> g <- sample(c("AA", "AB", "AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)

cft.mt> # Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
cft.mt> X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)

cft.mt> colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")

cft.mt> X[g == "AA", "B"] <- 0

cft.mt> X[g == "BB", "A"] <- 0

cft.mt> X[g == "AB",] <- X[g == "AB",] / 2

cft.mt> # Transform noisy X
cft.mt> xi <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)

cft.mt> a0 <- c(0,0)+0.3

cft.mt> A <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)

cft.mt> A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))

cft.mt> Z <- t(a0 + A %*% t(X + xi))

cft.mt> # Add noise to Y
cft.mt> eps <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)

cft.mt> Y <- Z + eps

cft.mt> layout(matrix(1:4, ncol=2, byrow=TRUE))

cft.mt> xlab <- "Allele A"

cft.mt> ylab <- "Allele B"

cft.mt> lim <- c(0,6)

cft.mt> plot(X, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim)
Waiting to confirm page change...

cft.mt> points(Z, col="blue")

cft.mt> points(Y, col="red")

cft.mt> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c("X", "Z", "Y"), col=c("black", "blue", "red"), title="Variables:", bg="#eeeeee")

cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> # Fit model
cft.mt> # - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
cft.mt> alpha <- c(0.10, 0.075, 0.05, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001)

cft.mt> fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98)

cft.mt> Ms <- fit$M

cft.mt> col <- terrain.colors(length(Ms))

cft.mt> #col <- rainbow(length(Ms))
cft.mt> col[length(Ms)] <- "red"

cft.mt> lim <- c(-0.5,5)

cft.mt> plot(Y, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim, main="Y")

cft.mt> for (kk in seq(along=Ms)) {
cft.mt+   M <- Ms[[kk]]
cft.mt+   points(M, pch=19, cex=2.5, col=col[kk])
cft.mt+   lines(M, col=col[kk], lwd=2)
cft.mt+   text(M, cex=0.8, labels=kk)
cft.mt+ }

cft.mt> legend("topright", pch=19, pt.cex=2, legend=c(alpha, "final"), col=col, title=expression(alpha), bg="#eeeeee")

cft.mt> apex <- which.min(apply(M, MARGIN=1, FUN=function(u) sum(u^2)))

cft.mt> a0hat <- M[apex,]

cft.mt> Ahat <- M[-apex,]

cft.mt> Ahat <- apply(Ahat, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))

cft.mt> if (sum(Ahat[c(1,4)]^2) < sum(Ahat[c(2,3)]^2)) {
cft.mt+   Ahat <- matrix(Ahat[c(2,1,4,3)], nrow=2)
cft.mt+ }

cft.mt> Ainv <- solve(Ahat)

cft.mt> Xhat <- t(Ainv %*% (t(Y) - a0hat))

cft.mt> cat("True A:\n")
True A:

cft.mt> print(A)
          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 0.9938837 0.1240347
[2,] 0.1104315 0.9922779

cft.mt> cat("Estimated A:\n")
Estimated A:

cft.mt> print(Ahat)
          [,1]      [,2]
[1,] 0.9921387 0.1448959
[2,] 0.1251428 0.9894469

cft.mt> plot(Xhat, cex=0.8, xlab=xlab, ylab=ylab, xlim=lim, ylim=lim, main=expression(hat(X)))

cft.mt> x1 <- par("usr")[2]

cft.mt> y1 <- par("usr")[4]

cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,0), col="red", lwd=2)

cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,0), y=c(0,y1), col="red", lwd=2)

cft.mt> lines(x=c(0,x1), y=c(0,y1), col="blue", lwd=2)

cft.mt> plot(X[,1], Xhat[,1], cex=0.8, xlab=expression(X), ylab=expression(hat(X)), xlim=lim, ylim=lim)

cft.mt> points(X[,2], Xhat[,2], cex=0.8, col="red")

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
Ok, one more thing excluded. In the meantime, I have updated the
AllelicCrosstalkCalibration class and the cfit() of 'sfit' so that we
can get more verbose output. I've uploaded these updates as patches.
Do the following to grab them [as explain online as well]:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

From now on, the patches apply everything you load the library (until
a newer version is installed).

Then, in the analysis script you are using, tell aroma.affymetrix to
show more output while calibrating for allelic crosstalk:

acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=-55)

You should see something like:

processed on many different data sets, on different computers and

AllelicCrosstalkCalibration class and the cfit() of 'sfit' so that we
can get more verbose output.  I've uploaded these updates as patches.
Do the following to grab them [as explain online as well]:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

From now on, the patches apply everything you load the library (until
a newer version is installed).

Then, in the analysis script you are using, tell aroma.affymetrix to
show more output while calibrating for allelic crosstalk:

acc <- AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
csC <- process(acc, verbose=-55)

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
I am really puzzled with this one. Everything looks right, but it
seems like the external call to 'sfit' either fails or does not
complete, because when trying to read for "pipe", there is nothing
there. What is your operating system, Windows XP Professional,
Windows Vista, ...? Also, under what privileges are you running this,
admin, super user, safe user?

If you don't have the right to run everything that could explain it.
However, since it worked with the bare-bone example(cfit.matrix), that
is an unlikely explanation though.

I wonder if there are some side effects from loading aroma.affymetrix
that cause the problem. What if you do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
library(sfit)
example(cfit.matrix)

Would that still work?

I have one more thing we could try, and I think it is worth
understanding what goes wrong, and I'm sure the answer is "obvious"
when we find it. I'll return to you with that 2nd test, but I'll run
some torturing tests on my WinXP machine to see if I can push it to
give an error.

FYI, if you've got the data calibrated for crosstalk on your Linux
machine, you should be able to use that output (copy the files or use
the same shared directory) on Windows. The package will detect that
the files are already there and skip the fitting (meaning it will
never call 'sfit').

/Henrik

On 2/15/08, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:

I am really puzzled with this one.  Everything looks right, but it
seems like the external call to 'sfit' either fails or does not
complete, because when trying to read for "pipe", there is nothing
there.  What is your operating system, Windows XP Professional,
Windows Vista, ...?  Also, under what privileges are you running this,
admin, super user, safe user?

If you don't have the right to run everything that could explain it.
However, since it worked with the bare-bone example(cfit.matrix), that
is an unlikely explanation though.

I wonder if there are some side effects from loading aroma.affymetrix
that cause the problem.  What if you do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
library(sfit)
example(cfit.matrix)

Would that still work?

I have one more thing we could try, and I think it is worth
understanding what goes wrong, and I'm sure the answer is "obvious"
when we find it.  I'll return to you with that 2nd test, but I'll run
some torturing tests on my WinXP machine to see if I can push it to
give an error.

FYI, if you've got the data calibrated for crosstalk on your Linux
machine, you should be able to use that output (copy the files or use
the same shared directory) on Windows.  The package will detect that
the files are already there and skip the fitting (meaning it will
never call 'sfit').

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
Sorry I forget to mention I am admin user of XP professional system.
 
Yue
On 2/15/08, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:

I am really puzzled with this one.  Everything looks right, but it
seems like the external call to 'sfit' either fails or does not
complete, because when trying to read for "pipe", there is nothing
there.  What is your operating system, Windows XP Professional,
Windows Vista, ...?  Also, under what privileges are you running this,
admin, super user, safe user?

If you don't have the right to run everything that could explain it.
However, since it worked with the bare-bone example(cfit.matrix), that
is an unlikely explanation though.

I wonder if there are some side effects from loading aroma.affymetrix
that cause the problem.  What if you do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
library(sfit)
example(cfit.matrix)

Would that still work?

I have one more thing we could try, and I think it is worth
understanding what goes wrong, and I'm sure the answer is "obvious"
when we find it.  I'll return to you with that 2nd test, but I'll run
some torturing tests on my WinXP machine to see if I can push it to
give an error.

FYI, if you've got the data calibrated for crosstalk on your Linux
machine, you should be able to use that output (copy the files or use
the same shared directory) on Windows.  The package will detect that
the files are already there and skip the fitting (meaning it will
never call 'sfit').

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
Ok, now we're definitely on to something.

I've updated the cfit.matrix() patch to also show the contents of the
temporary data file generated. Please download the patches again:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

Then, try the following so we can rule out a few things...

Test #1: (Repeated calls)

library(aroma.affymetrix)
library(sfit)
example(cfit.matrix)
for (kk in 1:10) {

fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98, verbose=TRUE)
}

Does that given an error? If not, proceed...

Test #2: (Fitting with a much larger data set)

# Number of data points (N=1000 in the cfit example).
N <- 2e6

# Simulate genotypes
g <- sample(c("AA", "AB", "AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)
# Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)
colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")
A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))

fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98, verbose=TRUE)
}

Does this give an error?


Test #3: (Back to your data again)
With this new patch revealing even more output, retry with

process(acc, verbose=-55)

It should give an, but what is the output?

/Henrik

# Number of data points (N=1000 in the cfit example).
N <- 2e6

# Simulate genotypes
g <- sample(c("AA", "AB", "AB", "BB"), size=N, replace=TRUE)

# Simulate concentrations of allele A and allele B
X <- matrix(rexp(N), nrow=N, ncol=2)
colnames(X) <- c("A", "B")
X[g == "AA", "B"] <- 0
X[g == "BB", "A"] <- 0
X[g == "AB",] <- X[g == "AB",] / 2

# Transform noisy X
xi <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)
a0 <- c(0,0)+0.3
A <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
A <- apply(A, MARGIN=2, FUN=function(u) u / sqrt(sum(u^2)))
Z <- t(a0 + A %*% t(X + xi))

# Add noise to Y
eps <- matrix(rnorm(2*N, mean=0, sd=0.05), ncol=2)
Y <- Z + eps

str(Y)

for (kk in 1:10) {
fit <- cfit(Y, dump=2, alpha=alpha, q=2, Q=98, verbose=TRUE)
}

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
At least, the law of elimination took as a bit closer. Yet again, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

then

options(troubleshoot="saveAll", troubleshootPrefix="fileA")

and call process(acc, verbose=-55).

You will now get three (compressed) files in the working directory
[getwd()] that saved the state of the function and the data:

fileA01.Rbin
fileA02.txt
fileA03.Rbin

The first two are the largest and about 5-10MB each. If you can make
these available on a webserver, please do that and let me know the
URLs. Otherwise, email them to:

hb-large [at] braju [com] com

I'll see if I can reproduce the problem given those files.

/Henrik

On 2/15/08, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:

At least, the law of elimination took as a bit closer.  Yet again, do:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

then

options(troubleshoot="saveAll", troubleshootPrefix="fileA")

and call process(acc, verbose=-55).

You will now get three (compressed) files in the working directory
[getwd()] that saved the state of the function and the data:

fileA01.Rbin
fileA02.txt
fileA03.Rbin

The first two are the largest and about 5-10MB each.  If you can make
these available on a webserver, please do that and let me know the
URLs.  Otherwise, email them to:

hb-large [at] braju [com] com

I'll see if I can reproduce the problem given those files.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
Hi,

I've been trying to figure what is going wrong, but I cannot reproduce
it. The files you've sent me show that there is nothing strange with
the data being fitted. My best guess is that the external algorithm
is launched but somehow it chokes and gives up resulting in an "empty"
output. The only way forward I can see is to narrow down the problem
using the actually machine that cause the problem. If someone else
gets/can reproduce the same problem that will give lead to go forward.

So, unfortunately there is nothing more I can from my side, and I have
to leave this as a open problem/bug (of the 'sfit' package).

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with 'sfit' package (Was: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Error in process() function when test programm in "Total Copy number analysis(5.0&6.0)")
parts:
Thank you for your help, I really appreciate it.  Since the Linus version seems to work, it is not a big problem for me now.
 
  Thanks again,
 
 Yue

On 2/25/08, Henrik Bengtsson <h...@stat.berkeley.edu> wrote:

Hi,

I've been trying to figure what is going wrong, but I cannot reproduce
it.  The files you've sent me show that there is nothing strange with
the data being fitted.  My best guess is that the external algorithm
is launched but somehow it chokes and gives up resulting in an "empty"
output.  The only way forward I can see is to narrow down the problem
using the actually machine that cause the problem.  If someone else
gets/can reproduce the same problem that will give lead to go forward.

So, unfortunately there is nothing more I can from my side, and I have
to leave this as a open problem/bug (of the 'sfit' package).

/Henrik
